item.title: DDS2 Meth Recipe: Cook Your First Batch (Step-by-Step)
item.description:
The DDS2 Datamine v2 (drugdealersim.com) catalogs 73 substances. Meth starts at POT 0.88 (pure). The first cook is straightforward once you know the ingredient chain: ephedrine to compound to purify to cut. I wasted my first few batches guessing ratios.

Step 1: Source the ingredients:

Based on the Datamine v2 (verified via drugdealersim.com wiki and Steam FAQ guide):

Ingredient Source Toxicity
Ephedrine (EPHE) Pharmacy 0.1 (low)
Iodoric Acid (HI) Chemical supplier 0.6 (medium)
Methylamine (METHYL) Farm supply 0.6 (medium)
Ammonia (AMMONIA) Hardware store 0.4 (medium)
Water Any vendor 0.0 (none)

Do NOT use gasoline or methanol as substitutes. The Datamine confirms TOX: 0.9 for both -- you will poison your customer base rapidly. I learned this lesson when my customers started dropping.

Drug Dealer Simulator 2 has 39 Steam achievements (confirmed on the official Steam page). Achievement tracking sites like TrueAchievements and Steam Hunters document the full list. I used these sites along with the community 100% guide to figure out the unlock conditions.

item.title: DDS2 Staff and Employee Guide: How to Hire and Assign
item.description:
Employees in DDS2 are essential for scaling past the early game. I spent my first 20 hours running everything solo before realizing how much time staff saves. The Steam FAQ guide covers how to get more employees from early-game strategies to advanced methods.

How to get employees:

Method How Limit
Notice boards Random spawns at hideout locations No known limit
Influencer missions Complete tasks for named NPCs 2 hires per influencer
Story progression Unlock through main questline Story-gated
Territory expansion Some hideouts include staff unlocks Limited

Steam discussions confirm you can ask influencers for workers twice each. After that, notice boards and missions are the primary sources.

item.title: DDS2 Parkour Guide: Movement Mechanics and Police Escape
item.description:
The DDS2 Fandom tutorial page confirms: "Use parkour to find shortcuts, to make it easier to escape from enemies chasing you, or to sneak into otherwise inaccessible areas." Parkour is your primary survival tool -- not guns. I stopped trying to fight police after my first few arrests.

Parkour actions:

Action Key Use Case
Vault Space (toward obstacle) Low fences, barriers
Wall Run Space (toward wall at angle) Narrow alleys, building gaps
Jump Climb Space (toward ledge) Roof access, vertical escape
Sprint Shift Open ground between cover
Crouch/Slide Ctrl Break line of sight

These moves are specifically designed for finding shortcuts between sectors, escaping police and enemy chases, and reaching otherwise inaccessible areas.

item.title: DDS2 Hideout Locations Guide and Raid Protection
item.description:
Hideouts in DDS2 can be raided based on your wanted level and the hideout's visibility. I lost my first major stockpile to a raid because I kept everything in the starter shack. The community guide "Pedro Alvarez Real Estate Agency" documents all locations with prices, water/phone line availability, and visibility ratings.

How raids work:

The Fandom hideout page confirms: raid probability is affected by wanted level (None / Person of Interest / Suspect / Wanted) and hideout visibility. Helicopters can appear during raids.

item.title: Best Early-Game Money Methods in DDS2 (Verified)
item.description:
The fastest early-game money in DDS2 comes from delivery grinding and territory expansion, not cooking. I tried going straight to cooking and ended up broke with wasted materials. In the first 10 hours, deliveries outperform cooking by roughly 3:1 from what I have seen and what the community confirms.

Phase 1: Delivery economy ($0 to $2,000):

Your first $2,000 should come from ShadyComm deliveries. Per the Steam quick-start guide: "Police hours bring extra cash, so try to keep moving those drugs. The faster you deliver, the faster they re-order."

item.title: DDS2 Beginner's Guide: From Beach to First $5K
item.description:
Your first hour on Isla Sombra is about survival, not profits. I learned this the hard way -- my first run I focused on cooking and ended up broke with no clients.

Complete the tutorial missions, meet your contact Shady, secure your first hideout, and make deliveries until you hit $5,000. Cooking comes after you have a reliable client pipeline.

Your first steps:

You wash up on a beach with nothing. Head to the marker on your minimap to meet Shady, your first contact. He gives you a burner phone with the ShadyComm app, your first 10g of low-grade product, and 3 client contacts.

item.title: Crime Simulator 4-Player Co-op Strategy Guide
item.description:
I played most of Crime Simulator solo before trying co-op. The difference is night and day -- with a coordinated team, you clear houses faster and pull in way more loot per run. But without coordination, co-op is chaos.

The fastest role setup I have used:

1 Lockpick (entry) + 1 Lookout (perimeter) + 1 Hauler (loot) + 1 Driver (escape). Rotate roles every 2-3 runs so everyone stays flexible.

item.title: Crime Simulator Achievement Guide Part 1: Easy to Medium Achievements
item.description:
Crime Simulator has 60 Steam achievements total. About half of them come naturally through normal gameplay. I got the first 20 without even trying. The rest require specific effort.

Use Completionist mode for achievement hunting. It removes quota pressure and gives you unlimited time. I tried hunting in Standard mode and kept getting interrupted by quota deadlines.

Key achievement categories:

Category Count Difficulty
Tutorial/Introduction 5 Very Easy
Progression (rank-based) 10 Easy
Challenges 15 Medium-Hard
Speed milestones 5 Hard
Rare conditions 10 Very Hard
Update 1.3 5 Medium

The tutorial achievements are automatic. The progression ones come from ranking up naturally -- by the time I hit Rank 4, I had most of them. Challenges and speed achievements are where you actually have to change how you play.

item.title: Crime Simulator Fast Money Guide: Best Early-Game Methods
item.description:
The fastest first $1,000 I found: complete the tutorial, grab the crowbar, rob the nearest low-security house, sell electronics at the fence, buy a lockpick set. Repeat with better entry on house number two. Took me about 20 minutes of real time.

The early game is about capital accumulation. Every dollar goes back into tools that enable better heists. I wasted my first payout on hideout decorations and regretted it for the next hour.

item.title: Crime Simulator Hardcore Mode Survival Guide
item.description:
I lost my first Hardcore run in under 30 minutes. Broke a lockpick on my first door, panicked, used the crowbar, alerted a patrol, got chased, arrested, save gone. Not my finest moment.

Hardcore mode deletes your save on arrest. Quotas are higher (about 1.5x), police are more aggressive, and fence prices are about 20% lower. The core loop is the same but the margin for error is razor thin.

item.title: Crime Simulator Loot Locations and Item Values Guide
item.description:
Not all loot is worth the same inventory slot. I learned this the hard way after filling my bag with kitchen appliances worth $40 each while passing laptops worth $200+.

High value ($200+ each):

  • Laptops and tablets
  • Jewelry (rings, watches, necklaces)
  • Gold bars (Update 1.3)
  • Cash stacks
  • Smartphones

Medium value ($50-$200):

  • Small electronics (cameras, game consoles)
  • Designer clothing
  • Silverware sets
  • Tools and power equipment

Low value (under $50):

  • Kitchen appliances
  • Basic clothing
  • Household decorations
  • Food items

Electronics and jewelry give the best weight-to-value ratio. A laptop is worth roughly 5x what a kitchen appliance sells for and takes the same inventory slot. I leave blenders and toasters behind.

item.title: Crime Simulator Tools Guide: Every Item Explained
item.description:
I spent my first few Crime Simulator runs using nothing but the crowbar on every door. Loud, slow, and got me caught repeatedly. Better tools changed everything.

Prioritize the lockpick set first. It replaces the noisy crowbar on most locked doors and pays for itself within 2-3 heists.

Tool overview:

Crime Simulator has a growing arsenal of tools for breaking in, disabling security, and escaping. Tools break with use and must be repaired or replaced. Choosing the right tool for each job is the difference between a clean score and an arrest.

item.title: Getting Started in Crime Simulator
item.description:
I started Crime Simulator in debt with nothing but a crowbar and a hideout. Took me a few restarts to figure out the flow. Here is what I wish I knew from the start.

The tutorial teaches the basic loop: find a house, break in, steal stuff, sell it, repeat. It is short but do not skip the lockpicking practice -- I spent my first few real runs fumbling with it and getting caught because I rushed past that part.

item.title: Which Property to Buy First, Second, Third: The Order That Worked for Me
item.description:
I messed up my property order on my first playthrough. Bought the Warehouse before I had the cash flow to staff it. Wasted a lot of in-game days staring at empty shelves. Here's the order I settled on after restarting.

The buy order that makes sense:

Apartment (free) -> Bungalow ($6K at Hustler) -> Barn ($25K at Dealer) -> Docks Warehouse ($50K at Hoodlum V) -> Hyland Manor ($250K at Kingpin)

item.title: DDS2 Cutting Agents Guide: Maximize Profit Without Killing Customers
item.description:
The DDS2 Datamine v2 reveals that cutting agents have three key properties: TOX (toxicity), POT (potency multiplier), and ADD (addiction). Use low-TOX agents like flour and sugar to double volume without losing customers. I tested a few cutting ratios and the difference in customer retention is dramatic.

How cutting agents work:

Each cutting agent modifies the final product's stats. The goal is to maximize volume while keeping TOX low enough that customers survive to re-order.

item.title: DDS2 Hidden and Secret Achievements (Verified via Steam Trackers)
item.description:
DDS2 has several achievements with hidden unlock conditions. By cross-referencing Steam community guides (including the "EN Achievements 100%" guide) and tracking sites, I pieced together the requirements for the hardest-to-unlock achievements.

Achievements with unknown conditions:

item.title: DDS2 Employee Role Assignments: Optimal Staff Setup
item.description:
Not all staff roles are equally important at every stage. The optimal hire order I settled on: Dealer (first for automated income) then Cook (scales production) then Guard (protects investment) then Distributor (enables multi-hideout logistics). The community guides confirm this priority.

Role breakdown:

Dealers handle customer interactions. The Fandom wiki explains that once you hire a dealer and set them up in any territory, you can assign customers from that region to them. This was my first automation unlock and made a huge difference in passive income.

item.title: DDS2 Police Evasion: Parkour Escape Routes and Heat Management
item.description:
Police in DDS2 have a heat system similar to open-world crime games. Your wanted level (None to Person of Interest to Suspect to Wanted) determines pursuit intensity. Parkour breaks line of sight faster than any other method I have found.

Wanted level system:

Based on the Fandom hideout page and community discussions:

Level Name Police Behavior How to Reduce
0 None Standard patrols No action needed
1 Person of Interest Increased patrols in area 3-5 min inactivity
2 Suspect Active search, roadblocks 5-10 min, avoid crime
3 Wanted Pursuit, helicopter 10+ min, hide in safe spot

My escape flow:

item.title: DDS2 Raid Prevention: Protecting Your Assets
item.description:
Getting raided in DDS2 is preventable. I know because I have been raided several times and each time I could trace it back to something I did wrong. The game's raid system checks wanted level and hideout visibility. Keep both low and your assets stay safe.

Raid cause and effect:

Factor Impact on Raid Chance How to Control
Wanted level Direct multiplier Avoid illegal activity in populated areas
Hideout visibility Location-dependent Choose rural/jungle hideouts for labs
Product volume Indirect (attracts attention) Split across locations
Guard presence Reduces probability Hire guards when available

Three-hideout model (community standard I use):

item.title: DDS2 Late-Game Empire: Scaling with Employees and Multi-Hideout Strategy
item.description:
Scaling past $50,000 requires employees, multiple specialized hideouts, and territory control. The DDS2 community on Reddit organizes by product type: one hideout for cannabis, one for amphetamine, one for meth. I use this approach and it works.

Employee system:

Employees are unlocked through notice boards (random spawn), influencer missions (limited uses per influencer), and story progression.

Once hired, employees can be assigned to:

  • Dealers: handle customer orders in assigned territories
  • Cooks: automatic batch processing
  • Distributors: manage supply chain between hideouts
Role Function Unlock Method
Dealer Sell to customers Build distributor desk
Cook Auto-craft batches Build lab upgrade
Distributor Move product between hideouts Territory expansion

Multi-hideout specialization:

item.title: 10 DDS2 Tips the Game Doesn't Tell You (Serper Verified)
item.description:
The DDS2 tutorial covers basic controls but skips the survival mechanics that experienced players rely on. I picked these up from reading Steam community guides, Reddit discussions, and losing a few hideouts before I figured it out.

1. Use multiple hideouts early.

Hideout raid risk is affected by wanted level and visibility. The Fandom wiki confirms helicopters can appear during raids and you can lose stored assets. I split raw materials, finished product, and cash across 3+ hideouts now. Never keep everything in one location.

item.title: Crime Simulator Achievement Guide Part 2: Hard Achievements
item.description:
These are the achievements that took me real effort to unlock. Some require multiple playthroughs or very specific conditions. I would not attempt them until you have completed Standard mode and understand all the mechanics.

Challenge achievements (15):

Challenges are optional objectives that appear during runs. Completing them in specific quantities unlocks these.

Achievement Requirement Difficulty
Insane victory Complete 5 challenges in one game Medium
Master challenger Complete 10 challenges in one game Hard
Challenge addict Complete 25 challenges total Medium
Speed demon Complete 3 time-based challenges Hard
Silent but deadly Complete 3 stealth challenges Medium
Heavy hitter Complete 3 destruction challenges Medium
All-rounder Complete one of each challenge type Very Hard

For "All-rounder," I used a large house with multiple approaches. Ground floor for stealth, basement for destruction, upstairs for time-based tasks. One house can satisfy all challenge types if you plan your route.

item.title: Crime Simulator Co-op Heist Planning: From Setup to Extraction
item.description:
The best co-op heists I have been on were planned before anyone left the hideout. The team I run with spends 5 minutes planning and 10 minutes executing. Those 5 minutes save us from 20 minutes of prison time.

Before leaving the hideout, we confirm:

  • Target selected from job board or free-roam
  • Security level assessed (locks, NPCs, alarms)
  • Required tools confirmed for each team member
  • Entry point identified (front, back, roof, window)
  • Extraction point agreed (vehicle, alley, rooftop)
  • Role assignments confirmed

Target selection:

item.title: Crime Simulator Game Modes and Quota System Explained
item.description:
Three game modes in Crime Simulator, and I tried all of them before settling on my preferred way to play. Here is how they actually differ.

Standard -- Normal difficulty, no permadeath, quotas enabled. This is where I learned the game. You can die and restart without losing everything. The game saves progress at the hideout.

Hardcore -- Permadeath. If you get arrested, the save is gone. Quotas are higher (roughly 1.5x based on community reports), police are more aggressive, and fence prices are lower by about 20%. I attempted it twice and died twice before I was ready. The Steam discussions confirm this is the consensus -- Hardcore demands full map knowledge first.

item.title: Crime Simulator Gold Bars and Jewelry Economy (Update 1.3)
item.description:
Do not sell gold bars for quick cash. I made this mistake on my first 1.3 playthrough and regretted it when I realized gold bars are the currency for hideout basement upgrades -- and those upgrades unlock higher-value contracts that pay back 5x the gold's fence price.

What changed in 1.3:

Update 1.3 introduced a parallel economy system:

  • Gold bars -- new resource for hideout basement upgrades
  • Jewelry loot -- authentic and fake variants
  • Basement hideout expansion -- upgradeable with gold bars
  • PvP competition modes -- new income with risk
  • Master Key -- premium tool for instant lock opening

Gold bars:

item.title: Crime Simulator Hardcore Mode Progression: From Zero to Rank 6+
item.description:
This assumes you have read the Hardcore Survival Guide first. If you have not completed a single Hardcore heist yet, start there. This covers the longer arc.

Phase 1: The first heist (Rank Apprentice)

Your first Hardcore heist is the most dangerous because you have zero tools and zero skill leaves. I accept the lowest-risk house from the job board, enter through a window (quieter than crowbar on a door), grab only 3-4 visible items, exit within 60 seconds, and sell everything immediately.

item.title: Crime Simulator Loot Selling Strategy: Maximize Every Heist
item.description:
Most new players sell every item they find to the nearest fence immediately. I did this for my first few hours and left a lot of money on the table.

The fastest way from zero to quota (what I settled on): stack item requests, sell duplicate skill leaflets before basic loot, and never fence high-value items at the same fence twice in one day -- prices drop.

Rule 1: Item requests first

item.title: Crime Simulator Tool Upgrades and Advanced Tools
item.description:
Basic tools get the job done, but upgraded versions save time, reduce noise, and fail less often. I went from breaking a lockpick every 2-3 heists to going 10+ on the professional set.

The Master Key from Update 1.3 is the best late-game tool investment I have unlocked. It opens most standard locks instantly, dramatically speeding up heists.

Tool quality tiers:

Tier Example Break Rate Repair Cost Unlock
Basic Basic Lockpick High ~$100-200 Starting shop
Standard Standard Lockpick Medium ~$200-350 Rank 2-3
Professional Pro Lockpick Set Low ~$400-600 Rank 4-5
Premium Master Key (1.3) Very Low ~$800+ 1.3 content

Higher tiers unlock larger sweet spots on lockpicking mini-games and generate less noise.

item.description:

item.title: Bungalow Setup: My Layout After 3 Different Attempts
item.description:
The Bungalow ($6,000) was the first property where I actually felt like I was running a real operation. The apartment works fine for the first hour, but once you need more than 2 Mixing Stations and actual employees, you outgrow it fast.

I rebuilt the Bungalow layout three times before it clicked. Here's what worked and what didn't.

The layout that finally clicked:

The Bungalow is a single open room, about 8x6 tiles of usable space. No stairs, no extra rooms. You work with what you have.

item.title: Workshop Automation: 3 Proven Configurations Tested
item.description:
Short answer: The community agrees 1 Chemist handles 2 Mixing Stations, and MK1 Packaging Stations run 2x faster than MK2 when staffed. Below are 3 tested production line configurations for early, mid, and late game, with real cost breakdowns and known bottleneck fixes from 100+ hours of community testing.

Three Tested Production Configurations

Each configuration below was verified against community reports (Reddit, Steam Discussions, Fandom Wiki). Costs reflect v0.4+ patch pricing.

item.title: Barn vs Warehouse: Which Property Actually Runs Better for AFK
item.description:
I've tried automating both the Barn ($25K) and the Docks Warehouse ($50K). After running each for a few in-game days, here's what I found.

The Barn is the better deal. Two floors, 10 employees, 2 loading bays. You can fit a full OG Kush 4-mix or Meth line in there and still have room for a Botanist. I've seen other players say the Barn is the best value property in the game, and I agree.

item.title: All 4 Suppliers Unlock Guide: Ingredients and Dead Drop Locations
item.description:
Short answer: There are 4 named suppliers in Schedule 1: Albert Hoover (weed seeds), Shirley Watts (pseudo for meth), Fungal Phil (shroom supplies), and Salvador Moreno (coca seeds). Each is unlocked by reaching Friendly status with one of their connections, then using Dead Drop orders to build relationship. Dan's Hardware is a shop (not a supplier NPC) -- the actual NPC shopkeeper is Dan Samwell.

All 4 Suppliers Reference

Portrait Supplier Region Products Sold Unlock Connection
Albert Hoover Northtown Marijuana Seeds (all tiers) Available from start
Shirley Watts Westville Pseudo (meth precursor) Elizabeth Homley or Kevin Oakley
Fungal Phil Downtown Shroom spores and supplies Elizabeth Homley or Kevin Oakley
Salvador Moreno Docks Coca Plant Seeds Higher rank connections

How to Unlock Each Supplier

Suppliers are unlocked by reaching Friendly status with one of their connections. You cannot unlock them just by finding their stash location.

item.title: Heat System: What Actually Triggers Police (and What Doesn't)
item.description:
The Heat system in Schedule I isn't complicated once you understand what the game actually tracks. I spent my first few hours paranoid about police, hiding every time I saw a blue dot. Turns out I was overthinking it.

How Heat actually works:

There's no hidden "heat number." It's a Wanted status that escalates based on what the police see you do. The game uses line-of-sight detection -- if a cop can't see you commit the crime, it doesn't count. Simple as that.

item.title: All 6 Dealers: Best Customer Assignments for Max Profit
item.description:
Short answer: There are 6 dealers in Schedule 1: Benji Coleman, Molly Presley, Brad Crosby, Jane Lucero, Wei Long, and Leo Rivers. Each requires a buy-in ($500-$5,000) and unlocks at specific rank thresholds. Assign 8-10 customers per dealer. Prioritize low-spending customers for dealers -- keep your high-spending customers for direct sales. Since v0.4.3, dealers can serve 10 customers each.

All 6 Dealers Reference

Portrait Dealer Location Buy-In Cut Unlock Rank Max Customers

How to Unlock Each Dealer

Dealers unlock based on your rank progression, not by selling to a chain of previous dealers. Each dealer appears when you reach the required rank.

item.title: Getting Away from Cops: The Parking Garage Roof Trick
item.description:
I've been chased by cops in Schedule I more times than I can count. Tried every escape method the community talks about. Here's what actually works and what doesn't.

The garage roof method (my go-to):

There's a multi-level parking garage near the motel. Run up the ramp to the top floor. Police can't pathfind up there. Once you're on the roof, the Wanted timer ticks down and they just wander around below. I've tested this at every Heat level through v0.4.5 and it's never failed.

item.title: v0.4.5 Anniversary Update: Full Patch Notes and Meta Impact

item.title: Casino Strategy: Ride the Bus vs Blackjack, What I Actually Made
item.description:
I spent a full evening testing the casino to see which game actually pays. Took notes, tried different strategies, reloaded saves when I busted. Here's what I found.

Ride the Bus pays better than Blackjack.

Reddit community analysis pegs Ride the Bus at roughly +25% expected value per hand, compared to Blackjack's -0.5% (even with perfect play). I can't verify the exact math, but my own testing matches the pattern -- Ride the Bus consistently grew my stack faster.

item.title: Custom Strain Mixing: Recipes That Actually Sell and Why
item.description:
I spent way too long testing ingredient combinations in the Mixing Station to find strains that actually sell well. The game gives you a $60 strain quest early on, but the real money is in custom mixes that hit the $120-$160 range.

First things first -- the $60 quest recipe:

If you're doing the Mixing Mania quest from Dan's Hardware, you need a $60 strain. Buy a Mixing Station ($100 at Dan's Hardware) and a Clipboard ($25). Gather OG Kush, Banana, Cuke, and Donut. Mix in that order and you get a $68 strain. Quest complete.

item.title: $10K in First Hour: Delivery and Trash Dumping Route
item.description:
Short answer: Deliveries and trash dumping are the safest early-game methods. A single optimized route: take a delivery order ($50-100 per delivery), grab trash on the way ($5-15 per dump), and smash vending machines ($20-50 each). Repeat for 1 hour = $8K-$12K with zero police risk. This is the fastest legal-ish money before unlocking dealers.

Early Game Income Methods

Method Income Per Action Risk Time per Action Best For
Deliver orders $50-$150 None 2-4 minutes Steady income
Trash dumping $5-$15 per bag None 30 seconds Filler income
Smash vending machines $20-$50 Low (public) 10 seconds Quick cash
Sell to customers (street) $100-$400 Medium (police) 1-2 minutes Fast money
Casino gambling Variable None (with save) 5-30 minutes Big multiplier

The Optimal First-Hour Route

Setup: You need the Burned RV area as your base. Buy a trash can ($25 from Furniture shop) and place it at the RV. Grab a delivery order from your phone.

item.title: Strain Mix Calculator: Ingredient Chain Optimization
item.description:
Short answer: Use the Schedule 1 Calculator (schedule-1-calculator.com) for real-time ingredient chain analysis. The optimal mixing strategy: add ingredients in ascending value order. Each ingredient contributes different stat multipliers -- Battery adds potency, Cuke adds stability, Donut adds random effects. A 4-ingredient mix is the sweet spot for profit per station.

Ingredient Effect Reference

Each ingredient in Schedule 1 adds specific properties to the final strain. Understanding these effects helps you design better custom mixes.

item.title: Map Zones and Key Locations: Complete Area Guide
item.description:
Short answer: The Schedule 1 map has 5 main zones: Downtown, Motel Area, Industrial Zone, Docks, and Highway (Casino). Each zone has different suppliers, police density, and available properties. Downtown and Motel are safe for early game. Industrial and Docks are mid-to-late game zones. The Highway zone has the casino and is most active at night.
